title: Scarcity: The Rule of the Few
coreMove: Remove the loss pressure long enough to price the option by its use, not its disappearance.
sourcePressure: The source supports scarcity, fewness, limited access, urgency, threatened loss, and the defense of separating actual value from the pressure created by disappearing availability.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not make this a general fear-of-missing-out chapter; it is about value swelling under threatened loss.

exampleSpecs.audience: a renter offered the last available plot
exampleSpecs.stakes: accepting a plot she cannot maintain because last available feels precious
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she covers the last plot label and compares the watering schedule to her actual week before accepting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated plot map clipped to a chain-link fence

exampleSpecs.audience: a collector considering a signed atlas
exampleSpecs.stakes: overpaying because the dealer says another buyer is circling
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the collector asks to inspect condition notes and comparable sales after hearing only two left in private hands
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cotton gloves resting on a velvet-lined case

exampleSpecs.audience: parents offered a deposit window for a preschool slot
exampleSpecs.stakes: paying a nonrefundable deposit before checking fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one parent repeats the deadline, then asks what they would choose if two slots were open for a week
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sticky note with the deposit deadline beside a toy catalog

exampleSpecs.audience: a guitar repair technician tempted by a small-batch plane
exampleSpecs.stakes: buying a tool that duplicates one already on the bench
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the technician lays the current plane beside the preorder specs and checks what job the scarce tool would uniquely do
exampleSpecs.firstImage: curling maple shavings around a brass-bodied plane

exampleSpecs.audience: a township resident offered limited early installation
exampleSpecs.stakes: locking into a plan because access has been scarce for years
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the resident compares plan terms before and after the installer says the first trenching round closes Friday
exampleSpecs.firstImage: orange utility flags lined along a gravel road

exampleSpecs.audience: a painter offered one substitute spot with a fast reply deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: pausing paid work for a residency that no longer fits her goals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the initial thrill, she reads last year's studio requirements and realizes the substitute spot is scarce but misaligned
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a voicemail transcript printed beside paint-splattered invoices

skillTargets: separate scarcity pressure from actual usefulness
recognize closing access as a value amplifier
decide under deadlines without ignoring fit
evaluate whether a scarce option deserves its new urgency

tryThisNowSpec: When something is framed as almost gone, cover the scarcity cue and say the one use or benefit that would still justify it tomorrow.
